deep.reconstruction:
The page has two small coloured sketches and no prose. Each shows a local piece of an arrangement of pseudo-lines in orange: two crossing pairs (X shapes) with two nearly vertical lines between them. The lines are labelled at their lower ends λ, α, β, μ, with small arrows pointing to the ends. A light-green curve crosses the whole configuration transversally. Grey pencil hatching marks a region. A thick dark segment between points x_0 and x_1 lies on a dashed horizontal line just below the green curve.

In Figure 1 the green curve runs roughly straight and passes below the vertex of the left X. A short dark bar at the green level and the bar x_0x_1 below it both sit inside the triangle cut out by the two crossing lines. In Figure 2 the green curve has been pushed up into a bump over the left crossing point; the vertex is marked with a dark dot. The segment x_0x_1 is now the full base of the triangle bounded by the two crossing lines and the dashed line, and the hatching has moved below.

The previous page supplies the vocabulary. There a 'découpage' (cutting curve, drawn as a blue dotted line) separates a 'région générisée I' from a 'région spécialisée II'. It also speaks of an 'arc de spécialisation pour I, de générisation pour II', and states that a move is gen→spec, or spec→gen / gen-spec, 'suivant qu'on rencontre un triangle, ou un sommet'.

So this page illustrates one elementary move of a cutting or sweeping curve (the green line) across a vertex of the pseudo-line arrangement. Before the move the cut meets the triangle below the vertex. After the move the vertex has passed to the other side of the cut. The degenerate position in between, where the cut passes through the crossing point, is the 'special' configuration (a triple point). The two sides are its generic neighbours.

In modern terms this is the passage through a codimension-one stratum in the space of arrangements of n+1 pseudo-lines, the extra line being the cut. Equivalently it is a triangle flip (Ringel move) involving the cut and the two crossing lines. It is also a single step in a topological sweep of the arrangement. Grothendieck phrases it as specialization/generization in a stratified 'moduli' of arrangements. The segment x_0x_1 tracks the edge of the cut that is replaced during the flip. The page belongs to his 1983–84 attempt to build a combinatorial/stratified theory of pseudo-line systems, consistent with the tame-topology outlook of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical claims are made on this page, so nothing can be checked for correctness. The figures are consistent with a triangle flip of the cut past a vertex.
Labelling is incomplete: the right-hand X lines are unlabelled. Figure 2 has no Greek labels, so line identities must be inferred from Figure 1.

ideas.what: Moving a transversal cut (sweep curve) across a vertex of a pseudo-line arrangement, viewed as passing through a special (degenerate) configuration between two generic ones.
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation in simple pseudo-line arrangements; elementary step of a topological sweep; wall-crossing in the stratified space of arrangements (cf. higher Bruhat orders B(n,2))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flip connectivity; Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ~1980–84); Edelsbrunner–Guibas (topological sweep, 1986/89); Manin–Schechtman (1989) for higher Bruhat orders
ideas.where_published: Pseudo-line systems are only alluded to in general terms (tame topology programme in the Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); the specific notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Specialization/generization language (from scheme theory) applied to cells and regions of an arrangement relative to a cut.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization order on strata of a stratified space (face poset / Bruhat-type order on arrangements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory; combinatorial version in oriented matroid theory (Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler)

deep.surprise_reason: These are illustrative figures of a standard elementary move: a cut or sweep line passing over a crossing, i.e. a triangle flip. They belong to Grothendieck's unpublished pseudo-line notes. The specialization/generization framing is characteristic of him, but this page contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: Figure 1 has two dark segments: a short one at the level of the green curve inside the left triangle, and the labelled one x_0–x_1 on the dashed line below. The arrows point to the lower ends of the lines labelled λ, α, β, μ.
In Figure 2 the crossing point at the top of the left X is marked with a dark dot, and a short tick lies just below it inside the green bump.
Grey pencil hatching marks regions: upper-left around the first X in Figure 1, below the dashed line in Figure 2. These are presumably the generized/specialized regions of the previous page.
